🚗 A Tool to Share: an AI-Built Car Cost-of-Ownership Calculator

By Will Zheng · July 5, 2026 · From Issue #17

A quick aside from the AI-and-workflows theme. Most car cost calculators miss two things. First, they ignore the time value of money on a car loan — the interest you pay, and the opportunity cost of the cash you tie up, materially change which car is actually cheaper. Second, a lot of people still run the old rule of thumb that a two-year-old car beats a brand-new one. Since COVID, the supply/demand shift in used-car pricing has repeatedly broken that rule: in two of my own recent car purchases, a new car actually penciled out cheaper than a two-year-old CPO once financing and total cost of ownership were modeled properly.

So I built a calculator that factors those in. Sharing it in case it helps your own decision-making:

Open the Car Cost Calculator →

Disclaimer: This calculator is provided for informational and educational purposes only, not financial advice. Figures are estimates and may contain errors — verify every number and assumption independently and at your own responsibility before making any purchase decision.
